question: How can tap water with trace PFAS lead to high blood levels?
answer: PFAS build up in the body over time: every glass adds a little, and little leaves. So water with just 4 parts per trillion, plus other exposure, can keep blood at 2 parts per billion, 500 times higher than the water.
move: Tiny doses that stay add up: trace water can keep blood high.

web.label: A blood level counter starts at 0 parts per billion beside a glass of tap water. Tapping keeps drinking water with 4 parts per trillion of PFOA, and blood rises toward 2 parts per billion. Asks how trace PFAS in tap water can lead to high blood levels.

source: Veritasium, “The Biggest Chemical Coverup In History” (YouTube, 2025)
